statements.label: supported
statements.text: METTL3 speeds up the maturation of pri-miR221/222, which lowers PTEN levels and ultimately drives the proliferation of bladder cancer.
statements.evidence: We confirmed the oncogenic role of METTL3 in bladder cancer by accelerating the maturation of pri-miR221/222, resulting in the reduction of PTEN, which ultimately leads to the proliferation of bladder cancer.
statements.note: The Results state that METTL3 accelerates pri-miR221/222 maturation, reducing PTEN and leading to bladder cancer proliferation.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In bladder cancer, METTL3 expression was significantly increased, and this elevated expression tracked with poor prognosis in bladder cancer patients.
statements.evidence: Moreover, we found that METTL3 was significantly increased in bladder cancer and correlated with poor prognosis of bladder cancer patients.
statements.note: The Results report significantly increased METTL3 in bladder cancer and a correlation between METTL3 and poor patient prognosis.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Bladder cancer patients with high METTL3 expression respond worse to cisplatin-based chemotherapy than patients with low METTL3 expression.
statements.evidence: The survival analysis was adopted to explore the association between METTL3 expression and the prognosis of bladder cancer.
statements.note: Survival analysis linked METTL3 expression to prognosis, but the abstract reports no analysis of chemotherapy or of any treatment response.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: METTL3 interacts with the microprocessor protein DGCR8 and regulates pri-miR221/222 processing in an m6A-dependent way, as shown by RIP, co-immunoprecipitation and m6A dot blot assays.
statements.evidence: RNA immunoprecipitation (RIP), co-immunoprecipitations and RNA m6A dot blot assays were conducted to confirm that METTL3 interacted with the microprocessor protein DGCR8 and modulated the pri-miR221/222 process in an m6A-dependent manner.
statements.note: These assays confirmed that METTL3 interacts with DGCR8 and modulates pri-miR221/222 processing in an m6A-dependent manner.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: METTL16 is the enzyme that places the N6-methyl mark on adenosine 43 (A43) of the human U6 snRNA.
statements.evidence: We demonstrate that METTL16 is responsible for N 6 -methylation of A43 of the U6 snRNA
statements.note: The abstract states directly that METTL16 is responsible for N6-methylation of A43 of the U6 snRNA.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The U6 position A43 sits inside the essential ACAGAGA box, a region that base-pairs with pre-mRNA 5' splice sites during splicing.
statements.evidence: Interestingly, A43 lies within an essential ACAGAGA box of U6 that base pairs with 5' splice sites of pre-mRNAs during splicing
statements.note: The abstract places A43 within the essential ACAGAGA box of U6, which base pairs with 5' splice sites of pre-mRNAs during splicing.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: CRAC experiments revealed that METTL16 associates not only with U6 snRNA and other ncRNAs but also with many lncRNAs and pre-mRNAs.
statements.evidence: METTL16 binds to the U6 snRNA and other ncRNAs as well as numerous lncRNAs and pre-mRNAs.
statements.note: The CRAC data showed METTL16 binding to U6 snRNA, other ncRNAs, and numerous lncRNAs and pre-mRNAs.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: METTL16 accounts for most of the human m6A sites that are installed independently of the METTL3-METTL14 complex.
statements.evidence: The identification of METTL16 as an active m 6 A methyltransferase in human cells expands our understanding of the mechanisms by which the m 6 A landscape is installed on cellular RNAs.
statements.note: The abstract establishes METTL16 as an active m6A methyltransferase but gives no estimate of what share of METTL3-METTL14-independent sites it installs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Upregulation of both circNSUN2 and HMGA2 was more common in liver metastasis tissues than in primary colorectal carcinoma tissues.
statements.evidence: Clinically, the upregulated expressions of circNSUN2 and HMGA2 are more prevalent in LM tissues than in primary CRC tissues.
statements.note: The abstract reports that upregulated circNSUN2 and HMGA2 are more prevalent in liver metastasis tissues than in primary CRC tissues.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Antisense targeting of circNSUN2 reduced liver metastasis in PDX metastasis models of colorectal carcinoma.
statements.evidence: The upregulated expression of circNSUN2 promotes LM in PDX metastasis models in vivo and accelerates cancer cells invasion in vitro.
statements.note: The PDX models tested the effect of upregulated circNSUN2, and the abstract only suggests circNSUN2 as a therapeutic target without reporting any targeting experiment.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In colorectal carcinoma patients with liver metastasis, circNSUN2 was frequently upregulated in tumor tissue and serum, and its upregulation predicted worse patient survival.
statements.evidence: circNSUN2, frequently upregulated in tumor tissues and serum samples from colorectal carcinoma (CRC) patients with liver metastasis (LM) and predicts poorer patient survival.
statements.note: The abstract describes circNSUN2 as frequently upregulated in tumor tissue and serum of CRC patients with liver metastasis and as predicting poorer survival.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cytoplasmic export of circNSUN2 was increased by its N6-methyladenosine modification.
statements.evidence: Importantly, N 6 -methyladenosine modification of circNSUN2 increases export to the cytoplasm.
statements.note: The abstract states that N6-methyladenosine modification of circNSUN2 increases its export to the cytoplasm.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The microproteins that localize to mitochondria are required for normal mitochondrial respiration in human cardiomyocytes.
statements.evidence: We associate these microproteins with diverse cellular processes and compartments and find that many locate to the mitochondria.
statements.note: The abstract reports that many microproteins locate to the mitochondria but describes no test of their role in respiration or any other mitochondrial function.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Several dozen microproteins are produced from lncRNAs that already have well-characterized noncoding functions.
statements.evidence: Importantly, dozens of microproteins are translated from lncRNAs with well-characterized noncoding functions, indicating previously unrecognized biology.
statements.note: The abstract states that dozens of microproteins are translated from lncRNAs with well-characterized noncoding functions.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Translational regulation of cardiac gene expression proved extensive and was organized according to specific biological processes.
statements.evidence: We show extensive translational control of cardiac gene expression, which is orchestrated in a process-specific manner.
statements.note: The abstract reports extensive translational control of cardiac gene expression, orchestrated in a process-specific manner.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Hundreds of microproteins not detected before, encoded by lncRNAs and circRNAs, were identified, and their protein products were confirmed in vivo.
statements.evidence: We identify hundreds of previously undetected microproteins, expressed from lncRNAs and circRNAs, for which we validate the protein products in vivo.
statements.note: The abstract reports hundreds of previously undetected microproteins from lncRNAs and circRNAs, with protein products validated in vivo.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In neurons lacking Cyrano, surplus miR-7 drives cytoplasmic destruction of Cdr1as, partly through increased slicing of Cdr1as by miR-671.
statements.evidence: Without Cyrano, excess miR-7 causes cytoplasmic destruction of Cdr1as in neurons, in part through enhanced slicing of Cdr1as by a second miRNA, miR-671.
statements.note: The abstract states that without Cyrano, excess miR-7 causes cytoplasmic Cdr1as destruction in neurons, partly via enhanced miR-671 slicing.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Degradation of miR-7 directed by Cyrano was far more effective than earlier reported cases of target-directed microRNA degradation, mostly from artificial and viral RNAs.
statements.evidence: Cyrano-directed miR-7 degradation is much more effective than previously described examples of target-directed microRNA degradation, which come primarily from studies of artificial and viral RNAs.
statements.note: The abstract says Cyrano-directed miR-7 degradation is much more effective than previously described examples, which come mainly from artificial and viral RNAs.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The Cyrano/miR-7/Cdr1as regulatory network operates the same way in human neurons as in mouse neurons.
statements.evidence: using gene editing in mice to probe the molecular consequences of disrupting key components of this network.
statements.note: All the described experiments used gene editing in mice, and the abstract makes no claim either way about human neurons.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Cyrano lowers miR-7 levels, which relieves repression of miR-7 target mRNAs and allows the circular RNA Cdr1as to accumulate.
statements.evidence: By reducing miR-7 levels, Cyrano prevents repression of miR-7-targeted mRNAs and enables accumulation of Cdr1as, a circular RNA known to regulate neuronal activity.
statements.note: The abstract states that by reducing miR-7, Cyrano prevents repression of miR-7 targets and enables Cdr1as accumulation.
